statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk is 22%, inside the 20-24% watch band and below the 25% block threshold.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH rather than a block. The narrow danger window spans 12:00Z-15:00Z on 1 October, covering initial jobless claims at 12:30Z, the U.S. cash open at 13:30Z, the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI at 13:45Z and ISM Manufacturing at 14:00Z. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ sets a fresh overnight high at 30,887.50 and clears its retracement-zone resistance on thin Golden Week volume; Tail firms to 22%
body: Observed state at the assessment cutoff: NQ Dec-26 futures last printed 30,881.25, plus 182.50 points or 0.59%, at 23:16 ET on roughly 37.15k Globex contracts, inside an overnight range of 30,684.50-30,887.50 and only about 6 points below that high against a 30,698.75 previous close. NQ has therefore extended from 30,838.00 an hour earlier, set a fresh overnight high, and is holding at that extreme. It has also cleared the 30,812.75 upper retracement-zone boundary flagged in market reporting published at 02:10Z. Extreme-holding plus a clean grind higher is a genuine amplifier and lifts Tail one point to 22%. The counter-evidence remains substantial. The whole Globex range spans only about 203 points, or 0.66%, on thin turnover, with Hong Kong and mainland China closed for National Day. The last completed cash session argues directly against a no-retracement regime: NASDAQ-100 closed 30 September at 30,408.50, plus 0.23%, which was the low of its 30,408.50-30,630.45 range after a late-session fade erased the entire intraday gain. That completed round trip is the most recent observed evidence on mean reversion, and it shows reversion working. The tape was rotational rather than aligned: the S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,651.54 and the Dow fell 0.86% to 50,906.05 while the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.24% to 26,861.06. Cross-asset backdrop: VIX settled at 16.34, up 1.87%, within a 15.62-16.61 range and near the low end of its 13.38-35.30 annual range. The Federal Reserve H.15 release for 29 September shows the 2-year at 4.89%, the 10-year at 5.26% and the 30-year at 5.59%; market reporting notes long yields holding above 5.30% despite August core PCE printing at 3.0% year on year and 0.2% month on month, with headline at 3.4%, all lighter than expected. Oil has eased further rather than tightened: WTI is near $89.54, down 0.97%, and Brent near $97.24, down 0.81%, after Saudi Aramco restored East-West pipeline flows and Middle Eastern exports reached their highest levels since late February, though ship-tracking estimates still put flows near two-thirds of pre-war levels and U.S.-Iran talks have yielded little progress. Falling oil and falling front-end yields are dis-amplifiers, not Tail amplifiers. Asia is firm but divergent: the Nikkei 225 trades at 68,355.81, plus 2.40%, near its own session high, led by AI and semiconductor names after Micron reported record fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $54.23B with non-GAAP EPS of $33.42 and guided fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue to $61.5B plus or minus $1.5B. Risk reading: the amplifier set is stronger than an hour ago but still incomplete. NQ holding a fresh overnight high counts, and the Asian semiconductor bid is aligned, but the Nikkei's 2.40% gain against NQ's 0.59% is a magnitude divergence rather than aligned index-wide one-way structure, the range is narrow on thin holiday volume, VIX is near annual lows, yields and oil are easing rather than confirming, and the last completed cash session faded entirely from its high. No persistent directional efficiency, shallow-pullback sequence or failed-retracement pattern has been observed on NQ. Tail therefore firms only to 22%, inside the watch band and below the 25% block threshold. Stress holds at 70%: elevated absolute yields and oil near $90 with an unresolved Hormuz backdrop keep the environment difficult, offset slightly by the softer oil print, against an event stack of jobless claims, the final manufacturing PMI and ISM Manufacturing today followed by September payrolls tomorrow. Confidence is 88% on a timestamped futures quote, a confirmed cash close, official H.15 yields, current oil and VIX levels, a live Asian session, a verified seven-day U.S. calendar and a confirmed 7 October FOMC minutes date. The shared Finviz context file was collected at 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with partial collection status, roughly 28 hours old and far outside the 90-minute freshness limit, so it was treated as stale and excluded; independent research carried the full evidence load.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opens in the green EA_ON band with Tail 15-16% and Stress 65-66% through the Asian and European hours of 30 September, firms from 11:00Z as the U.S. session approached, and crosses into the yellow WATCH band at 12:00Z with Tail 20%. Tail peaked at 23% across 15:00Z-16:00Z with Stress at 72%, then eased through the U.S. afternoon and overnight, settling at Tail 20-21% with Stress 70% and Confidence 88% through the small hours of 1 October. Dominant mode was mixed in all 24 available hours, Tail ranged from 15% to 23%, and Confidence held in an 85-88% band throughout.
outlookSummary: The published path keeps Tail inside the 20-24% watch band for all 24 forecast hours, so the mapped state stays WATCH and yellow throughout. Tail starts at 22% on the observed fresh overnight high, eases to 21% through the thin late-Asian and pre-European hours while Hong Kong and mainland China remain shut for National Day, firms to 22% from the European open, and builds to a conditional peak of 24% across 13:00Z-14:00Z where the U.S. cash open, the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI and ISM Manufacturing stack inside 45 minutes. Stress tracks that shape from 69% up to a 75% peak and back. Nothing beyond the current clock-hour is observed: every later hour states its structure conditionally, with the depth of the first retracement after the 12:30Z claims print and the behaviour of pullbacks after the cash open named as the decisive tells. The window closes near the band floor with a pre-payroll overhang, since September employment data lands at 12:30Z on 2 October, outside this forecast window. Confidence decays from 88% to 85% purely with forecast distance.
